Chlorophyll catabolite in senescing plant plastids. Opening the chlorin macrocycle is the committed step of chlorophyll breakdown and is required to avoid phototoxic intermediates. Plastid enzyme; aligns to this set only over the Rieske domain.
Plastid enzyme of chlorophyll b biosynthesis. Two successive hydroxylations turn the C7 methyl into a formyl group, which is exactly what distinguishes chlorophyll b from chlorophyll a.

Plastid inner-envelope enzyme, proposed to oxidise the C7 methyl of protochlorophyllide and to be coupled to protein import across the envelope. Its physiological role is less firmly established than that of PAO or CAO, hence medium confidence.

Biosynthetic intermediate of the aeruginosins, cyanobacterial peptides whose protease-inhibitory activity depends on the unusual arginine derivative Aeap. AerC builds the pyrroline ring of Aeap from the prenylated agmatine made by Aer3, so this is a biosynthetic enzyme in a secondary metabolite pathway, not a degradative one. The set reaches cyanobacteria otherwise only through SxtT and GxtA.
